second_note: Evaluation uses the public pre-2026 Gibson and HM3D v1/v2 ObjectNav episodes (Habitat Challenge 2022 setting, Sec. IV-A) with no contamination or overlap check reported.

Each Dyad variant is compared with GRPO/GiGPO 'using the same LLM and RL training environment for each pair' (Sec. 5.1) under the shared hyperparameters of Table 10 (App. B.4); no selection on scored evaluation items is reported.

The headline ALFWorld result uses the public ALFWorld benchmark (2021) verbatim, with other pre-2026 public sets (WebShop, SWE-bench Verified, MMLU-Pro), and no contamination or overlap check is reported (Sec. 5.1, App. B.1).

Headline results mix reference types: the literature audit uses codes from two researchers' independent coding and adjudication (Sec. 3.3), timing results use measured verified outcomes of physical execution (Sec. 7.1-7.2), and Jev correctness on the constructed tasks is scored by programmatic task predicates (Sec. 6.2, Sec. 9).

Models are named with version tokens only (Jev-1.13 / Jev-1.13.0, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, GLM-4.7-Flash, Qwen3.5-4B; Sec. 7, Tables 7-11) with no revision or dated snapshot and no run dates, an incomplete version per the model-name rule.

Sec. 6.4 and Sec. 9 state that the questions and comparison families were formulated after the measurement records were inspected, a setting selected with feedback from the scored items (rule row 19), although all systems receive the same cases (Tables 8-12).

Thresholds and reduct picks are fitted on validation splits A/B before any test call (Sec. 5, Sec. 7.4), but the sensors get different disclosed request formats (one Noul question per value vs one JSON prompt per field, Sec. 6, App. B), a disclosed asymmetry.
